claims.title: Indigenous peoples of the grasslands
claims.summary: The Charrua and other hunting and gathering peoples occupy the plains north of the Rio de la Plata over many millennia, well before any European arrival.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-3000bce-indigenous-peoples-of-the-grasslands, claim TL:URY:event:3000bce:indigenous-peoples-of-the-grasslands, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Solis reaches the Rio de la Plata
claims.summary: The Spanish navigator Juan Diaz de Solis explores the estuary and is killed near its eastern shore; finding no gold, Spain largely ignores the Banda Oriental for nearly two centuries.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1516-solis-reaches-the-rio-de-la-plata, claim TL:URY:event:1516:solis-reaches-the-rio-de-la-plata, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cattle turn the plains to wealth
claims.summary: Cattle and horses introduced by early expeditions multiply across the grasslands into vast feral herds, drawing gauchos, hide-hunters and contrabandists to the frontier.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1611-cattle-turn-the-plains-to-wealth, claim TL:URY:event:1611:cattle-turn-the-plains-to-wealth, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portugal founds Colonia del Sacramento
claims.summary: Portuguese soldiers establish Colonia opposite Buenos Aires; it becomes a strategic outpost and smuggling centre, changing hands between the crowns for over a century.

sources.label: Historic Quarter of the City of Colonia del Sacramento

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1680-portugal-founds-colonia-del-sacramento, claim TL:URY:event:1680:portugal-founds-colonia-del-sacramento, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Spain expels the Portuguese at Montevideo
claims.summary: A Spanish force under Bruno Mauricio de Zabala drives out a Portuguese garrison that had begun fortifying the bay of Montevideo, opening the way for a Spanish town.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1724-spain-expels-the-portuguese-at-montevideo, claim TL:URY:event:1724:spain-expels-the-portuguese-at-montevideo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Founding of Montevideo
claims.summary: Zabala formally establishes Montevideo as a fortified Spanish port to counter Portuguese expansion; it grows into the chief stronghold of the Banda Oriental.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1726-founding-of-montevideo, claim TL:URY:event:1726:founding-of-montevideo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Viceroyalty of the Rio de la Plata
claims.summary: Spain creates the new viceroyalty centred on Buenos Aires, drawing the Banda Oriental into its administration and stoking eastern resentment of the centralising capital.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1776-viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata, claim TL:URY:event:1776:viceroyalty-of-the-rio-de-la-plata, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colonia listed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The historic quarter of Colonia del Sacramento, blending Portuguese, Spanish and post-colonial architecture, is inscribed as a World Heritage site.

sources.label: Historic Quarter of the City of Colonia del Sacramento

claims.title: Artigas and the Federal League
claims.summary: Jose Gervasio Artigas leads the Orientals against Spain and builds a federal league of provinces, championing autonomy against Buenos Aires across the Banda Oriental and beyond.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1815-artigas-and-the-federal-league, claim TL:URY:event:1815:artigas-and-the-federal-league, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Portuguese invasion and Artigas in exile
claims.summary: Portuguese forces from Brazil invade the Banda Oriental; after three years of resistance Artigas is defeated in 1820 and goes into permanent exile in Paraguay.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1816-portuguese-invasion-and-artigas-in-exile, claim TL:URY:event:1816:portuguese-invasion-and-artigas-in-exile, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The Thirty-Three Orientals declare independence
claims.summary: Juan Antonio Lavalleja and the Thirty-Three Orientals, having landed that April, proclaim separation from Brazil and union with the United Provinces, reigniting the war for the province.

sources.label: Uruguay: The struggle for national identity

claims.title: Treaty of Montevideo creates Uruguay
claims.summary: Under British mediation, the Preliminary Peace Convention ends the Argentine-Brazilian war by establishing the contested territory as the independent buffer state of Uruguay.

claims.title: Massacre of the Charrua at Salsipuedes
claims.summary: Government forces ambush and massacre the Charrua at Salsipuedes, a campaign that destroyed them as a distinct people and is remembered as a foundational injustice.

claims.title: The Guerra Grande
claims.summary: The rivalry of Colorados and Blancos erupts into the Guerra Grande; the Blanco Oribe besieges Montevideo for nine years while the Colorados, aided by foreign legions, hold the city.

sources.label: Uruguay: The struggle for national identity

claims.title: End of the long war
claims.summary: The Guerra Grande ends without outright victory, leaving Uruguay exhausted but independent and its two-party rivalry entrenched.

sources.label: Uruguay: The struggle for national identity

claims.title: Cattle economy and immigration
claims.summary: Booming exports of hides, beef and wool, British-built railways, and waves of Italian and Spanish immigrants remake Montevideo and the countryside.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1860-cattle-economy-and-immigration, claim TL:URY:event:1860:cattle-economy-and-immigration, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Batlle y Ordonez becomes president
claims.summary: Jose Batlle y Ordonez of the Colorado Party wins the presidency, beginning the reform era that would make Uruguay an early welfare-state democracy.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1903-batlle-y-ordonez-becomes-president, claim TL:URY:event:1903:batlle-y-ordonez-becomes-president, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: The great reforms
claims.summary: In his second term Batlle enacts the eight-hour day, free education, pensions, nationalisations, abolition of the death penalty and church-state separation, founding the model welfare state.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1911-the-great-reforms, claim TL:URY:event:1911:the-great-reforms, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: A new welfare constitution
claims.summary: A reformed constitution entrenches the secular, democratic and social character of the Batllista republic, including a plural executive to check one-man power.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1917-a-new-welfare-constitution, claim TL:URY:event:1917:a-new-welfare-constitution, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Terra's authoritarian interlude
claims.summary: Amid the Great Depression President Gabriel Terra suspends the constitution in a self-coup; constitutional democracy is restored later in the decade.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1933-terra-s-authoritarian-interlude, claim TL:URY:event:1933:terra-s-authoritarian-interlude, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Rise of the Tupamaros
claims.summary: The leftist urban guerrilla movement of the Tupamaros forms under Raul Sendic, turning to robberies, kidnappings and assassinations amid economic decline.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1963-rise-of-the-tupamaros, claim TL:URY:event:1963:rise-of-the-tupamaros, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Military takes power
claims.summary: With the Tupamaros crushed and the country in crisis, the president dissolves parliament with military backing, beginning a civic-military dictatorship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1973-military-takes-power, claim TL:URY:event:1973:military-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Return to democracy
claims.summary: After elections in 1984, Julio Maria Sanguinetti is inaugurated president, restoring civilian rule and freeing political prisoners under an amnesty.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-1985-return-to-democracy, claim TL:URY:event:1985:return-to-democracy, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Frente Amplio breaks the duopoly
claims.summary: The left-wing Frente Amplio coalition wins the presidency for the first time, ending nearly two centuries of Colorado and Blanco dominance.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-2004-frente-amplio-breaks-the-duopoly, claim TL:URY:event:2004:frente-amplio-breaks-the-duopoly, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Cannabis and progressive reform
claims.summary: Under President Jose Mujica, Uruguay legalises same-sex marriage and becomes the first country in the world to fully legalise and regulate cannabis.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Uruguay: From the Charrua of the Banda Oriental and a contested frontier between the Spanish and Portuguese empires to Artigas and the Thirty-Three Orientals, the 1828 buffer state between Argentina and Brazil, the reforms of Batlle y Ordonez, the dictatorship of 1973-1985, and a stable, progressive democracy.", terralore.co/country/URY/chronicle#ev-2013-cannabis-and-progressive-reform, claim TL:URY:event:2013:cannabis-and-progressive-reform, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.
